key_insight: Strong adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers still show component-wise outer similarity when each profile is normalized by its value at a common outer location.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact way to compare and model APG boundary layers across very different pressure gradients and Reynolds numbers, improving turbulence-model assessment and profile reconstruction.
method: Built a benchmark from new DNS of a suction–blowing-induced separation bubble plus published APG profiles
Tested multiple existing APG normalizations against two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components
Used pointwise normalization at a common outer location y_s, with results highlighted at y_s = 0.5δ
evidence_signal: Across β_e = 0.04–180 and Re_θ = 530–19000, the six quantities collapse to a common outer shape, with velocity-defect collapse for y/δ ≳ 0.2 and Reynolds-stress collapse for y/δ ≳ 0.4.
watch_item: The similarity is outer-region and component-wise, so it should not be assumed to extend into the near-wall region or to replace a universal scaling law.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
